answer: LINE defines the first-order joint probability between vertices v_i and v_j as a sigmoid of the inner product of their low-dimensional embeddings: p1(v_i, v_j) = 1 / (1 + exp(-u_i^T u_j)), where u_i and u_j are the embedding vectors. This is a distribution over vertex pairs, and it is symmetric because the inner product is symmetric. The empirical probability is the normalized edge weight: p̂1(i, j) = w_ij / W, where w_ij is the weight of the edge between i and j and W is the sum of all edge weights (each undirected edge counted in both directions). LINE then minimizes the KL divergence between p̂1 and p1 to learn the embeddings.
confidence_reasoning: The sigmoid-of-inner-product form and the w_ij / W normalization match my recollection of Tang et al. (2015), but I am not certain of the exact normalization constant convention for undirected edges.
